name: Pipe Diameter Calculator
description: Calculate required pipe diameter from flow rate and target velocity.

seo.title: Pipe Diameter Calculator - Size Pipes
seo.description: Pipe Diameter Calculator — Calculate required pipe diameter from flow rate and target velocity with instant results & multiple unit support.

formula.explanation: D = √(4Q / (π × v)). Flow in m³/s, velocity in m/s; ×1000 converts m to mm.

content.introduction: Calculate the minimum pipe inner diameter for a given flow rate and design velocity. Essential for hydraulic pipe sizing in process and utility systems.

example.description: For 50 m³/h at 2 m/s target velocity, minimum diameter is 94 mm. Standard DN100 (114.3mm OD, ~102mm ID) would work.

faq.q: What standard pipe size should I select?
faq.a: Round up to the nearest standard DN/NPS size. For example, if calc gives 94mm, select DN100 (4-inch).

faq.q: What velocity should I design for?
faq.a: Water discharge: 2-3 m/s; suction: <1.5 m/s; compressed air: 6-10 m/s; natural gas: 10-20 m/s.

faq.q: What is the difference between nominal and actual pipe diameter?
faq.a: Nominal pipe size (NPS/DN) is a label, not a dimension. Actual outside diameter is fixed per size, while wall thickness varies with schedule (Sch 40, Sch 80, etc.), so inside diameter = OD - 2 × wall thickness. Always use the actual ID for flow and velocity calculations.

sections.heading: Unit Conversion for Pipe Sizing
sections.body:
**Diameter units**

- 1 inch = 25.4 mm
- 1 mm = 0.03937 inch
- DN 50 = NPS 2 (nominal labels, not exact dimensions)

**Flow rate units**

- 1 m³/h = 0.2778 L/s = 4.403 US gpm
- 1 US gpm = 0.2271 m³/h

**Velocity units**

- 1 m/s = 3.28084 ft/s

When sizing, convert all inputs to one consistent unit system (metric or imperial) before applying the continuity equation Q = V × A.
